chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Zur'a, from al-Mufaddal ibn 'Umar, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I stand [for night prayer] while I am doubtful about whether it is Fajr.' He said: 'Pray according to your doubt. When the dawn rises, perform the Witr [prayer] and pray the two [rak'ahs]. And when you stand [for prayer] and the dawn has already risen, begin with the obligatory [Fajr prayer] and do not pray any other [night prayer]. When you have finished, make up what was missed. And let this not become a habit, and beware that you do not inform your family of this, lest they pray according to that and do not pray at night.'

key_terms.أَوْتِرْ: Perform Witr (the odd-numbered prayer concluding night prayer)
key_terms.الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ: The two [rak'ahs of Fajr or additional night prayer]

ai.seo_question: What should one do with night prayer if they are unsure whether Fajr has risen?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) addresses the practical jurisprudence of doubt (shakk) during the transition from night to day prayers, emphasizing the principle of proceeding on the basis of certainty once dawn breaks. It highlights the importance of maintaining the distinct identity of the Fajr obligatory prayer while cautioning against the casual neglect of voluntary night prayers (Tahajjud) by family members who might rely solely on this concession. The instruction to keep it private from one's family reflects a scholarly nuance in preventing the generalization of a specific ruling into a habitual practice that diminishes spiritual diligence.
